Sühne.et: From Middle High German süene, suone, from Old High German suona, from Proto-Germanic *swōnō. Cognate with Dutch zoen (“kiss”).

s: Suhl (an independent town in Thuringia, Germany)
Suhl.et: From Old High German Sulaha, of which the second element is aha (“river, water”).

Suhle.et: 17th-century alteration (after the related verb suhlen) of older Sole f, Sol m, n, from Middle High German sol, from Old High German sol, from Proto-West Germanic *sol, from Proto-Germanic *sulą.

s: Der deutsche Name bleibt für immer geschändet, wenn nicht die deutsche Jugend endlich aufsteht, rächt und sühnt zugleich, seine Peiniger zerschmettert und ein neues, geistiges Europa errichtet.
The German name remains forever shameful if the German youth is not at last to rise up, to avenge itself and at the same time to atone; to shatter its torturers and to build a new, spiritual Europe.
[…] (der wechselseitige Burdermord sühnt die Mißhandlung des Vaters, mit der das vorhergehende Drama 'Oidipus' schloß) […]
[…] (the mutual fratricide serves to atone for the abuse of the father's mistreatment with which the previous drama 'Oedipus' ended) […]
